raw_source.text_snippet: Although allotopic expression of mtDNA has demonstrated to be able to ameliorate the phenotype of some mitochondrial diseases, it fails to alter the heterozygous pattern of pathogenic mitochondria. In contrast, the autonomous replicative capacity of the mitochondrial genome, combined with observations that linearized mtDNA damaged by DSBs undergoes rapid degradation, offers a potential strategy to reduce, or even eliminate, pathogenic gene copies [ 48 ] (Fig. 3 A).

raw_source.text_snippet: Of the 130 confirmed pathogenic mutations in human mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), only 31 could theoretically be corrected using C-to-T editing tools. In contrast, an additional 51 targets could be rescued through A-to-G conversions, including those responsible for LHON, mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and MELAS, and Leigh syndrome (Table 1 ).
